teacraft.guide.title: About Tea Craft
teacraft.guide.p0.head: Where tea comes from
teacraft.guide.p0:
Tea saplings: zombies may carry them, and always drop one when killed.

Finished tea is graded 1 to 5 by the temperature of the biome it grew in -- the colder, the higher the grade:
tropical 1, subtropical 2, temperate 3, boreal 4, polar 5.

Tea bushes in cold and freezing biomes need a campfire within 2 blocks, otherwise they will not grow. A bush that lacks heat shows: "It is too cold -- place a campfire nearby."

The grade sets how long the effect lasts: grade 1 for 20 minutes, 2 for 40, 3 for 60, 4 for 80, 5 for 100.
teacraft.guide.p1.head: Phoenix Dancong
teacraft.guide.p1:
No phantoms spawn and phantoms will not attack you.

Grants Haste III: an Efficiency V diamond pickaxe breaks deepslate instantly.

Lasts up to 100 minutes (depends on tea grade).
teacraft.guide.p2.head: Black Tea
teacraft.guide.p2:
Hunger drains 90% slower, and grants Regeneration II.

Lasts up to 100 minutes (depends on tea grade).
teacraft.guide.p3.head: Green Tea
teacraft.guide.p3:
Grants Speed II, and creepers and undead will not attack you unprovoked.

Lasts up to 100 minutes (depends on tea grade).
teacraft.guide.p4.head: Green tea process
teacraft.guide.p4: Fresh leaf -> Wither (drying tray) -> Kill-green (tea wok) -> Roll (rolling tray) -> Dry (tea wok) -> Charcoal bake (baking basket) -> Finished tea
teacraft.guide.p5.head: Black tea process
teacraft.guide.p5: Fresh leaf -> Wither (drying tray) -> Roll (rolling tray) -> Ferment (rolling tray) -> First bake (tea wok) -> Charcoal bake (baking basket) -> Finished tea
teacraft.guide.p6.head: Dancong process
teacraft.guide.p6: Fresh leaf -> Wither (drying tray) -> Shake (drying tray, sneak and pick it up to shake) -> Kill-green (drying tray) -> Ferment (rolling tray) -> Charcoal bake (baking basket) -> Finished tea
teacraft.guide.p7.head: Work blocks
teacraft.guide.p7:
Every work block holds up to 32 tea leaves at once.

Right-click to put leaves in; right-click again with an empty hand to take them out.

Shaking requires sneaking and right-clicking to lift the drying tray.
teacraft.guide.p8.head: Pottery: wheel and kiln
teacraft.guide.p8:
The potter^s wheel and the clay kiln must be placed next to each other.

Put clay balls in the wheel, choose a piece, and click -- it goes straight into the kiln.

Put 8 fuel items into the kiln to start firing.
teacraft.guide.p9.head: Ceramic pieces
teacraft.guide.p9:
Tea cup: 1 clay ball
Gaiwan: 2 clay balls
Kettle: 4 clay balls
teacraft.guide.p10.head: Tray and vessels
teacraft.guide.p10:
A crafted tea tray is empty -- you add the gaiwan and cups yourself.

Hold a cup or gaiwan and right-click a slot to place it; empty-hand click a vessel to take it back.

Empty-hand click the tray rim (away from any vessel) to pick up the whole tray with everything on it.
